newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bosnia PM says world too slow in reconstruction aid.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia PM says world too slow in reconstruction aid.

text.p: Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic said on Friday the world was moving too slowly to aid his country's reconstruction and consolidate peace.

"The world can do much and there was a promise to extensively support Bosnia-Herzegovina's economic rehabilitation and reconstruction. And everybody knows that there will be no lasting peace without economic rehabilitation," Muratovic told Reuters in an interview during a summit meeting of central and eastern European leaders.

"We may understand some failure in the organisation (of aid) but we expect now for the next donor conference a more concrete approach to projects and we expect more co-financing of larger projects," he added.

Muratovic spoke after delivering a speech to a two-day summit meeting in Austria of the Central European Initiative grouping of central and eastern European states in which he criticised the slow pace of reconstruction in war-ravaged former Yugoslavia.
"The reconstruction so far had disappointing results when rehabilitation of industry and creation of jobs are concerned," the Bosnian Moslem prime minister said in the speech.

"The most sensitive problem of the reconstruction programme is that a number of pledges from donor conferences held in Brussels has not been fulfilled, and every excuse is used by certain donors to justify delays in implementation of their donations," he added.
An international donor conference in April in Brussels pledged $1.8 billion for Bosnia's post-war reconstruction.

Muratovic told Reuters that about half that amount had been disbursed, but he declined to identify the donors whose money had not been received, saying it would be released at the next donors' meeting.
"We have analysis but when we show analysis some donors are not very happy with it," he said. "So at the next conference there will be very detailed analysis of donation and of implementation."

Muratovic also took issue with critics such as the U.S. special envoy in Bosnia, Richard Sklar, who said in a newspaper interview that donor money was arriving slowly not only because of bureacratic procedures but also because of the "government's transfer of money to various accounts".
"This is really up to donors how to use their money," Muratovic said.
The CEI, which admitted Moldova at its summit meeting, groups 16 central and easter European countries to deal with political, economic and social issues.
